newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SPANISH-BULGARIAN GROUP TO BUY BULGARIA CEMENT PLANT.
newsitem.headline: SPANISH-BULGARIAN GROUP TO BUY BULGARIA CEMENT PLANT.

text.p: The Spanish-Bulgarian investment consortium Marvex Ltd has been chosen as a buyer of 70 percent of Bulgaria's Devnya Ziment cement plant for $44.5 million, the consortium said on Thursday.
"In a protocol of the Privatisation Agency of March 18 the Marvex bid for 70 percent of Devnya Ziment has been put in the first place," said a Marvex statement faxed to Reuters.
Marvex pledged to invest $209.5 million in the plant over the next five years, the statement said.
It said Marvex had been worried on the short term for finalising the privatisation deal, which Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency had fixed in a letter to Marvex from March 24 until April 7.

Marvex representative to Bulgaria Yasen Vasilev said the consortium had not yet received a project for an agreement which has to settle all legal problems concerning the use of a nearby limestone quarry and the Black Sea port of Varna.
If the deal is not finalised within the term Marvex will lose its rights as a winner, he added.
"The term seems rather as an ultimatum because it also coincides with Easter holidays in Spain," Vasilev told Reuters.
Privatisation Agency officials were not immediately available for comment.
Vasilev said Marvex had been especially set up for the privatisation deal and the Spanish side, led by Moltiracion De Graneles was holding 80 percent in it.
The remaining 20 percent are held by the Bulgarian private company ELVA, which is the distributor of Russian Lada cars in Bulgaria, he said.
The Devnya Ziment plant, which exports 44 percent of its produce, had a turnover of 2.9 million levs in 1995.
Vasilev said Marvex planned to increase the plant's annual capacity to 4.5 million tonnes of cement in the next five years from the current 1.8 million tonnes.
"Marvex is willing to finalise successfully the deal and carry out its investment programme, which will guarantee the plant an access to new markets," the statement said.

On Monday Bulgaria's interim government approved the sale of 51 percent of another cement plant, Beloizvorski Ziment, to Swiss building materials group Holderbank Financiere Glarus AG for $32.5 million.
